messages:
Anya: quick heads-up — cedar-44k (int4hybrid) bring-up smoke. Running long-prefill runs and seeing a consistent, small token-level divergence after ~32k prefills. Not catastrophic but reproducible. :eyes:

Mike: can you paste the exact command + minimal logs so we can repro?

Anya: repro command below (runs on a single shard, quant profile=hybrid):
```bash
python -m bench.run \n  --model cedar-44k-int4hybrid \n  --quant-profile hybrid \n  --prefill 33000 \n  --prompt-file tests/long_prompt_50k.txt \n  --seed 42 \n  --batch 1
```

Anya: snippet from the run (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-23 09:12:02] prefill=32700 token=32789 divergence_detected: yes
perplexity(base=float32)=12.34 perplexity(quant)=13.23 delta=0.89
checksum_shard0=0x7f2a1c3b checksum_shard1=0x7f2a1c3b
```

Cheng: interesting — checksums equal up to the point of divergence? looks like internal state (KV/rotary) drifting rather than sharding mismatch. did you enable async-prefetch/cache-coalesce?

Anya: yes, async-prefetch=true and we have kv_cache_evict_threshold=0.85. I also tried prefetch=false and saw the divergence shift by ~120 tokens (later), so prefetch seems to affect timing.

Simone: could this be rotary scaling interaction with quant rounding? new quantizer v2 changed rounding mode for rot-sin/cos storage. Ops-bot rolled that out earlier: deploy note: quantizer/v2 @ 1749990000.

Julia: any diff in RoPE params between float and quant checkpoints? e.g., rope_scale or phase_shift constants?

Anya: model config lists rope_scale=1.00002 and rope_freq_clip=none in both, but the on-disk kv layout differs (packed int4 blocks). I ran a quick checksum pairwise per-kv-layer and saw a tiny CRC delta around layer 21 keys.

Mike: steps to triage: (1) run float32 vs int4hybrid with --prefill 33k and capture per-layer kv checksums at tokens 32k-33.5k, (2) disable async-prefetch and compare, (3) try quantizer v1 if available. Can you upload outputs?

Anya: uploading results to /tmp/cedar44k_checksums_1749991111.tar.gz (contains per-layer CSVs + run.log). Early look: layer21_key_crc_float=0x1a2b3c, layer21_key_crc_quant=0x1a2b3d (1-bit diff).

Cheng: 1-bit diff at a rotary-affecting layer could cause slow phase drift accumulating across tokens — that matches small perplexity delta. Try forcing rotary recompute on cast (store sin/cos as float16 at runtime) to confirm.

Simone: also compare with shard boundary alignment — if prefill length mod tile_size != 0, alignment + quant pack offsets could shift padding semantics. what's tile_size for int4hybrid?

Anya: tile_size=128 for current kernels. prefill=33000 -> 33000 mod 128 = 104, so not aligned. I'll run aligned run at 33024 (multiple of 128) next.

Mike: good. if aligned run removes divergence, we have a packing / alignment bug. if not, try float16-in-memory sin/cos fallback as Cheng suggested.

Anya: running both now. ETA ~20m. Will post concise diffs and a tiny reproducer script (prefill-snap.py) that extracts the KV at token T and serializes to jsonl for diffs.

Ops-bot: reminder — heavy long-prefill jobs should be tagged `long-prefill` so scheduler can avoid co-locating on noisy nodes.

Julia: brought-up note — also add a quick eval of token-prob drift on the public longbench set (just 100 samples) so we can quantify user-visible quality impact.

Anya: ack. plan of record: 1) aligned-run (33024) 2) async-prefetch=false run 3) runtime-fp16-sincos run 4) quantizer v1 test (if ops can roll back) 5) publish small report in /eng-ml/cedar44k/triage-1749991111.md

Mike: thanks, @Anya. tag me when logs uploaded. If we confirm alignment/packing, file a kernel issue and notify eng-runtime.

Anya: uploaded results and reproducer: /tmp/cedar44k_checksums_1749991111.tar.gz and /eng-ml/cedar44k/prefill-snap.py. Short summary: alignment run pushed divergence out by ~14k tokens but did NOT eliminate it. Next run will test fp16 sin/cos.
